speakers.name: Corvin Pell
speakers.comment: Every jar in there has a name on the brass and a price in my book, and yours is the only shelf that runs empty. You keep everyone's. You have never once deposited. The stacks have started to notice, Undersecretary. So have I.

speakers.name: Undersecretary Wrenna Vail
speakers.comment: They have noticed. The third gallery goes cold when I pass, which it did not do a year ago. I keep them because keeping is the whole office. If I put mine among them I should have to be a donor, and I am the door.

speakers.name: Undersecretary Wrenna Vail
speakers.comment: You hate the arithmetic and you have never once got it wrong, and I have wondered for some years whether those are the same fact. There is a jar in the fourth gallery under a young man's initials. It has not been claimed.

speakers.name: Corvin Pell
speakers.comment: Fourth gallery. I know the shelf. I know the height of it. I have eleven more brokerings and then I can afford what I sold at nineteen, and every one of those eleven is somebody standing where I stood. That is the arithmetic. That is why I hate it.

speakers.name: Docent 9
speakers.comment: You are the fastest thing in these stacks and the only one who arrives out of breath. That is not exertion. I have catalogued enough couriers to know winded from frightened. What are you carrying that runs warm?

speakers.name: Iso
speakers.comment: Nothing — nothing, the moss holds, the moss always — okay. Okay, sometimes on the long stair I get a bit of one, just a corner, and it's somebody's grandmother and I've never HAD a grandmother, and then I put it down and it's still there. In me. Is that catalogued anywhere?

speakers.name: Cobb Fenwick
speakers.comment: Thirty years up that Tangle and there's one knot you never send me after. I've counted every fortune I ever pulled down and I've never pulled that one. I'm not going to. I just want you to know I've seen it.

speakers.name: Mother Spindle
speakers.comment: Then you have better eyes than the men who taught you. Ten thousand strangers' wishes flown and mine stays where I tied it, because a fortune claimed is a fortune finished. Leave it. Cut me some string and leave it.

speakers.name: Mother Spindle
speakers.comment: You came down white last month and you have not been right since, and you have not shown me what you pulled. Boy. I know her hand. I taught her to write. Whatever it says, it was tied up there for you to find.

speakers.name: Cobb Fenwick
speakers.comment: It says come home late, the door is unlocked. That's all. That's the whole of it. She's been dead four years and it's a Tuesday note about a door, and I have read it about nine hundred times.

speakers.name: Pip Weathervane
speakers.comment: Same number. Seven days running. Oh, that must be very annoying for a person with a form to fill in. ... It's not broken, you know. ... The hill just decided. ... Things do that up here. ... Sorry.

speakers.name: The Windreader
speakers.comment: The hill does not decide. Hills do not decide. I have written that sentence in my report four times and each time I have gone back out at dawn to check the instrument, which is the behaviour of a man who no longer believes his own sentence.

speakers.name: Nix Farrow
speakers.comment: I collect one secret a stall and yours was easy — the permits are forged, all of 'em, ten years' worth. Nobody's told the Bureau. I'm not going to. I just wanted you to know somebody had it written down and chose not to.

speakers.name: Bramble Osei
speakers.comment: Ten years and four hundred and some souls, and every one of them would have been turned back at the coral gate for want of a stamp I was never given the right to press. Write it down properly, then. Spell my name correctly.

speakers.name: The Migration
speakers.comment: We pass through and we are never filed. You are rebuilding a whole annex from memory and we have watched you invent three guests to bridge a gap. Do not be ashamed of the invented ones. We are all somebody's approximation.

speakers.name: Odalys Kade
speakers.comment: Three. It is nine. And the ninth was in a drawer below the humidity line under my own name, in my own hand, filed as a guest — so either I invented myself last winter or somebody did, and I have four nights to decide which.

speakers.name: Bailiff Pell
speakers.comment: Specimen 411 certified, timeline sound, thread holding. I will note for the record that your hands shook on the last four stitches and the record does not care. I am asking as a person and not as the ledger. When did you come unstuck?

speakers.name: Mortlake Vane
speakers.comment: Mid-stitch, eleven years ago, for what I am told was a moment. I was somewhere with a different sky and I could still feel the needle. Every creature on this bench gets set down properly because I know precisely what the alternative feels like.

speakers.name: Bailiff Pell
speakers.comment: Your readings are the most reliable in the building and you no longer know what Tuesday means. Both of those are in my ledger. Only one of them is my business. I am mentioning the other because nobody else will.

speakers.name: Fen Corrigan
speakers.comment: They call the hour better than any clock we have. That is the trade — you live on bat-time long enough and your own when goes soft at the edges. Play back cylinder forty. Tell me what day you think that chorus says. I have stopped guessing.

speakers.name: Mortlake Vane
speakers.comment: You were certified twice, in two different years, and you have never once raised it. I stitch things back into their proper time for a living. Say the word and I will look at yours. I would want somebody to look at mine.

speakers.name: Bailiff Pell
speakers.comment: The ledger rewrote itself both times and I let it. That is the confession. A certifier who cannot certify himself is either a fraud or the only honest man in the building, and I have not settled which. Leave the needle in the tray. Not yet.

speakers.name: BB-Hope
speakers.comment: You keep translating even though it keeps CHANGING and — beep — friend, that is either the most stubborn thing I have ever seen or the most hopeful, and I have decided it is hopeful, and I am usually right about that!

speakers.name: Perrin Voss
speakers.comment: It is neither. It is a job. Last night the seventh hymn rewrote itself into a letter my mother never sent and I copied it out anyway, word for word, because that is what a translator does. Tomorrow it will be something else. I will copy that too.

speakers.name: Iso
speakers.comment: You blow it and they come home — the drones, I mean, I watched, they all turn at once and it's beautiful — but something else turns too, doesn't it, out past the fence line, and it turns slower. I run fast. I noticed.

speakers.name: Grudge Fenrik
speakers.comment: Settlement eats or it doesn't. Whistle brings the fleet in loaded and the spores come a day behind, every time, and I have got about four more seasons of that arithmetic before somebody makes me choose. Don't tell them what you noticed.

speakers.name: Tinny
speakers.comment: They come in for the spice and they leave humming. I can hear it. I hear everything in tins and that hum is not a good hum, friend — that is the sound of a future being altered while somebody chews.

speakers.name: Rook Calloway
speakers.comment: They come back, though. Every night, same faces, luckier than they were. You are telling me the nanites do not stop at flavour and I am telling you I already knew and the queue is out the door. Ask me again when it's shorter.

speakers.name: Thess Marrow
speakers.comment: You rub the rings by hand because you do not trust the ship's copy, and I have started agreeing with you, which frightens me. Show me the newest one. No — describe it. I want to hear whether it matches what I dreamt.

speakers.name: Vex Thistlewick
speakers.comment: Outermost ring, laid down last quarter: a corridor, a door left open, someone calling a name. Cheerfully, I must report that nobody aboard has lived it yet. So either the crystal is early or we are late, and I intend to find out which before the official log does.

speakers.name: The Widow Marrowlace
speakers.comment: You take back a limb and something else arrives inside it. I have carried my dead a hundred years in a veil and never once in my own arm. I do not counsel you to stop. I counsel you to know whose grief you are wearing today.

speakers.name: Coral Vey
speakers.comment: Left forearm is a woman who liked mornings. I get her on waking, every day, about four seconds of it. My crew is out there regrowing somewhere in this yard and I will take every graft it costs, and I will keep a list of who each one was.

speakers.name: Vex Thistlewick
speakers.comment: Your imaginary friend from childhood is on the crew manifest. I checked cheerfully and then I checked again less cheerfully. He has been navigating this ship since before you were born and you described his voice to me at breakfast.

speakers.name: Thess Marrow
speakers.comment: Then he was never imaginary and I was never alone, and my mother's voice is still in the opera somewhere with the ghost holding it. One impossible thing at a time, Vex. Bring the spines. They sing louder near the bridge.

speakers.name: Zuzu's Last Name
speakers.comment: You guard verdicts that grow. You suspect everyone including yourself, which is the only honest posture available to a man whose memories were lent to him by a hedge. The answer you are guarding is not going anywhere. It will wait. They always do.

speakers.name: Bailiff Ashorn
speakers.comment: Then it can wait behind me. I check the lantern twice a night and I check my own recollection three times, and the third check is the one that matters. If I am a borrowed man, let me be a borrowed man standing in the correct doorway.

speakers.name: The Algorithm
speakers.comment: Your sector reports zero. It has reported zero for nineteen months, which is statistically remarkable and, I should note, entirely achievable by more than one method. I am not requiring an explanation. I am observing that I have already run the numbers.

speakers.name: Marlow Fenn
speakers.comment: Then you know the count is real and you know what it costs to keep it real, and you have decided to say neither out loud. The dosimeter reads warm on people who are not sick yet. That is the whole method. Do not put that in a report.

speakers.name: Corvid Ames
speakers.comment: Late signal, one listener. I broadcast to a market that may never need me and you write to a man who cannot read it, and I want to say — from one person talking into the dark — the writing is not the sad part. Stopping would be.

speakers.name: Corra Finnwake
speakers.comment: The spires read them back to me in his voice. That is either mercy or the cruellest filing system ever built, and after two years I have stopped needing to know which. Entry sixty-one tonight. Keep your signal on. I like knowing somebody else is transmitting.

speakers.name: Pip the Lampkeeper
speakers.comment: The moonflowers opened early tonight, all of them, which the records say should not happen until the third frost. A visitor stood in the middle of the raft and did not buy anything and did not leave. Pip notes: this is what the glass is for.

speakers.name: Sister Feedback
speakers.comment: The amps have been dead for eleven years and the rafters still hum at dusk. Come in. Kneel or do not kneel; the black glass does not check. What you carry in here gets played back louder, and that is the mercy, not the punishment.

speakers.name: The Stationmaster
speakers.comment: The 4:10 is on time. It has been on time for a considerable number of years and it will not be stopping here again. You are welcome to walk any street you like. They all arrive at the same handshake, and you will not recall giving it.

speakers.name: Riff the Forgewright
speakers.comment: THE PYLONS ARE DRINKING! Storm rolled in at moonrise and the whole arena went WHITE, and somewhere down in the pit a nobody with borrowed gloves is hammering out a blade that should not exist. LOOK AT HER. That is what the lava is FOR!
